findings.current: The fighter trembled slightly as one of its missiles launched.
findings.defect: The English assigns the slight tremor specifically to the fighter. The Korean describes a missile mounted on the fighter being launched with a slight tremor, without making the fighter the subject of the shaking.
findings.rationale: The source preserves the physical detail but does not state that the fighter itself trembled.
findings.replacement: With a slight tremor, a missile mounted on the fighter launched.

findings.current: If we launch anything too powerful and it gets redirected, the result could be catastrophic.
findings.defect: The English adds the specific mechanism that the attack will be redirected. The Korean only says that firing one large shot incorrectly could cause a catastrophe.
findings.rationale: The source leaves the manner of the misfire or failure unspecified; the prior teleportation incident does not authorize narrowing this line to redirection.
findings.replacement: If we fire something big and it goes wrong, it could cause a catastrophe.

findings.current: Ten battles, nine wins, one loss. By the numbers, it was certainly an impressive record.
findings.defect: This adds a second shorthand restatement of the ten-battle record. The immediately preceding dialogue already states ten battles, nine victories, and one defeat; the source has only one additional shorthand restatement before the assessment.
findings.rationale: The assembled English repeats the same record twice after the dialogue, whereas the Korean repeats it only once.
findings.replacement: By the numbers, it was certainly an impressive record.

summary: The chapter is largely faithful, but four localized source-fidelity defects remain: one physical-subject shift, one added mechanism, one causality shift, and one duplicated restatement.
